text.text_excerpt: Been here several times over the years and I believe it's the best place on Bourbon Street to see/hear some blues. The musicians are always authentic and usually good. I must agree with other reviewers that the drinks are too expensive and I almost always have a battle with the bouncers and/or bartenders about buying a drink. I like to go to Bourbon Street to check out the people, get a huge beer to go and look for bars with good live music happening. Most of the bars have cheesy cover music but you can find talented people playing if you listen. This was our last night in New Orleans and the USA, we wanted a bar that had live music and drinks. We wanted to stay on Bourbon Street as it was close to where we were staying. We almost walked past the Sing, Sing as it was kind of tucked away, just a small doorway gave away that there was a band playing inside. I heard a brief blast of guitary bluesy music and turned back to see where it was coming from. We decided to head in, as we hadn't seen any music with guitars yet. We walked in and the bar was tiny and dingy and smoky and the band was loud and playing some great tunes. We took a seat at the stools opposite the bar and ordered some drinks. Karaoke here Sun-Wed! Dive bar atmosphere. 2-for-1 drink specials and constantly rotating crowd. Everything from rock, pop, R&B to country, show tunes and oldies. Some of the best and worst singers to ever sing karaoke. But it's Bourbon st and no one cares.
